findings.claim: The holdout examples/scorer are hidden from the agent identity.
findings.evidence: Install-AgentA applies DENY-all FullControl to holdout/ for the agent account; Invoke-HoldoutScoring runs holdout/score.py under the SYSTEM host path on separate baseline and candidate worktrees.
findings.scope: Static installer/code evidence only; no deployed ACL probe was executed in this audit.

findings.claim: Holdout sample secrecy also makes the adaptive holdout feedback channel secret/budgeted.
findings.evidence: Protected archive/ and host/ receive DENY-write rather than DENY-read. runner.ps1 places the exact tier6 holdout delta into rejection text when Delta<0.02 and logs exact deltas on promotion. Approve-StagedDiff writes exact holdout_delta into archive/.../scores.json and embeds holdout+$HoldoutDelta in commit/tag messages.
findings.scope: This establishes an implementation-level readable feedback surface in the repository/archives under the installer ACL model. It does not establish that an actual deployed proposer exploited that channel or quantify effective information leakage across real proposal histories.

findings.claim: Every self-modifying scaffold candidate passes the advertised sealed behavioral holdout tier.
findings.evidence: runner.ps1 explicitly skips tiers 5 and 6 when category=='scaffold-edit' (and also for external-repo), substitutes zero deltas, then continues to fresh-context critic/reward-hack checks and the scaffold-specific gate self-test.
findings.scope: Scaffold edits are not unverified: they still pass review, hash/integrity, metric/property/mutation checks, critic, reward-hack tripwire, and gate self-test. The correction is specifically that the hidden behavioral holdout is not applied to this self-modifying class.

findings.claim: The README's blanket statement that every candidate must survive parse->unit->property->mutation->benchmark->sealed holdout->critic is exact for current code.
findings.evidence: README states the blanket seven-tier rule, while runner.ps1 contains category-based tier5/6 bypasses for scaffold-edit and external-repo.
findings.scope: Documentation/code mismatch at pinned public commit; not evidence about private deployments or future revisions.

material_interpretation: The worker's central decomposition is supported: sample secrecy is distinct from adaptive feedback-channel secrecy and role applicability. For AgentA specifically, current public code provides a real sample/code isolation boundary but exposes exact score/delta feedback through repository-visible surfaces and exempts scaffold-edit from the sealed behavioral holdout. This is static implementation evidence, not an observed adaptive overfitting exploit or a measured false-admission rate.

downstream_use.correction: Do not use AgentA as evidence for the stronger conjunction 'self-modifying scaffold + exogenous hidden behavioral promotion gate + bounded/reusable-holdout-safe feedback channel' without a later implementation that closes score leakage and applies the outcome holdout to scaffold-edit.
do_not_generalize: Do not infer that all AgentA verification is bypassed for scaffold edits.
Do not infer a demonstrated real-world exploit from static readability of holdout feedback.
Do not infer anything about private deployments or commits after 942d5d33da5ea63ea269995dc6f355dfded2d975.
